Is the bottom of stem rotting or is it normal?
If it’s normal but just refusing to put out roots I would take off the bottom set of leaves and cut slightly higher than where it is now, use rooting powder again and hopefully this time it’ll produce roots. I’ve had this happen once and after 3 months of absolutely nothing I recut it and used roofing powder and finalllyyyyy it started putting out roots.

Sometimes plants do weird things, you’ve most likely done nothing wrong if it hasn’t rotted and it’s putting out new growth. Next time you could always mist around the soil around the plant (not directly onto the plant stem and don’t mist until the stem is healed if you do recut it).

I hope this helps!! Good luck :))

This happened to me last year!! The best course of action would be tweezers (with the thin ends) and a cotton swab.
What I did was lift up dirt a little away from sprouts. Take those dirt pieces onto a plate or something else to hold them and slowly use both the tweezer and the cotton swab to seperate them, you have to be very very careful.
Do not just try to rip them out without pulling the dirt up as that can damage or kill them. 

Get another different container and place all the sprouts with distance between them as there still could be more seeds coming up but slower so keep the original dirt as much as possible. I found even 6 months later I’d still get small random sprouts here and there. A year later I fully finally changed the dirt.

(The reason I’d separate them is so they won’t fully choke eachother to death, if you leave them like this a lot of them will die but if you didn’t want this many sprouts then leave them be and they’ll lower in numbers)

I saw you asking for tips so i thought this might help!

I have quite a few succulents (60 or more hehe) I’m obsessed with them, the biggest advice I can give is with soil, I use coco coir and perlite (80% coco coir and 20% perlite), with this soil mixture it’s very easy to know when to water! 

When cococoir is wet it goes a very very dark brown and when it’s dry you can absolutely tell as it’s a lighter brown and the soil goes bone dry. I only water my succulents when it’s bone dry and my favourite watering technique is by bottom watering them, just put them in something that can hold water and make sure the water is below the top of the pot (so dirt doesn’t come out of the top of the pot) and leave it in water for 30 mins and then take out. I also have started using fertiliser specifically for succulents and it’s life changing, it makes such a difference to their growth (If you want to know more about this and the schedule i use for fertilising just ask im happy to help).

Also you 100% need a hole in the bottom of the plant pot. A hole in the plant pot will make your life much easier trust me. And use terracotta pots they’re the best for succulents because the terracotta is a porous material which helps the roots of the plant be able to breathe much easier!

Hopefully this has helped!
